learning_outcomes.text: Students know the individual components of a chassis, their properties, and their effects on driving behavior. They are able to explain and differentiate chassis systems. Furthermore, they can perform calculations based on vehicle parameters.
Students can design chassis systems and develop them for driving dynamics. They possess the necessary knowledge for the further development of chassis components for current vehicles.
Students master the methods and knowledge areas necessary in chassis development. They are able to critically examine the acquired knowledge in chassis development and apply it with justification.
Students can analyze current chassis concepts, evaluate them, and further develop them considering the current state of the art.

syllabus_topics: Simulation of driving maneuvers and vehicle testing
assessment_rules: ECTS credits are awarded based on a graded written exam. An ungraded experimental work involving 3 experiments with corresponding preparation and post-processing is also required.
bibliography: Pischinger, Seiffert: Handbuch Kraftfahrzeugtechnik; Vieweg Braunschweig, 2016
Matschinsky: Radführungen der Straßenfahrzeuge; Springer Berlin, 2007
